title: 20 Minute Beef Stock Pot
description: A fast, deeply flavoured beef stock base — perfect for rich stews, braises, and hearty sauces.

ingredients.notes: Don't add too much all at once — you can't take it out once it's in.

method.instruction: In a large pot over high heat, add olive oil. Cook onion, carrot, celery, and garlic for 3–4 minutes until softened and fragrant.
Add mushrooms, thyme, oregano, tomato paste, and brown sugar. Stir well and cook for 2 minutes until the paste darkens slightly.
Pour in the red wine and bring to a boil. Let it reduce by half, about 3–4 minutes.
Add beef stock, bring to a simmer, and cook for 10 minutes. Season with salt to taste.
While the stock simmers, mash the plain flour and unsalted butter together to form a smooth paste (beurre manié).
Whisk the butter-flour paste into the simmering stock to thicken. Continue simmering for 2–3 minutes until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
In a separate hot pan with a little oil, sear the diced scotch fillet over high heat until browned on all sides but still medium-rare in the centre, about 2–3 minutes.
Add the seared beef to the sauce, stir gently, and serve immediately over mashed potatoes, polenta, or buttered pasta.

notes.title: Wine Substitute
notes.content: If you prefer not to use wine, substitute with additional beef stock plus 1 tablespoon of balsamic vinegar for depth.

notes.title: Beurre Manié
notes.content: This butter-flour paste is a French technique for thickening sauces without lumps. Mix it thoroughly before whisking into hot liquid.

notes.title: Why Scotch Fillet
notes.content: Scotch fillet is ideal for this recipe because it stays tender during quick, high-heat searing. Tougher cuts like chuck or brisket need long slow braising and won't work in a 20-minute stock pot. If substituting, use rib-eye or sirloin — anything with good marbling that can be served medium-rare.
